clue.text: Record a way to dispose of rubbish

parts.note: a gramophone record is a disc
taken as written
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A council leaflet describing how to get rid of household rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: To discard is to throw away something unwanted, which is exactly what disposing of rubbish means.

clue.text: With half the month gone, I have to bluff

indicators.note: half of it gone means only part of the named word survives

parts.note: the month of the year at the end, the last month
the contraction I've

explanation.surface: Someone running out of time this month and forced to fake it.
explanation.walkthrough: The month here is the last of the year; losing half its eight letters leaves the first four.
explanation.definitionFit: To bluff is to mislead by pretence, the same as deceiving someone.

clue.text: Bad girl's put up a diamond perhaps for the trick

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a tart is a loose woman, and the 's makes it TART'S
taken as written
a diamond is an example of a gem

explanation.surface: A wicked woman staking a diamond in a game of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A stratagem is a cunning plan or ruse, a synonym for a trick.

clue.text: Convert needs no introduction to Pater

indicators.note: without an introduction a name loses its opening letter

parts.note: Walter Pater was the Victorian critic and essayist

explanation.surface: A religious convert hardly needs introducing to a priest called Father.
explanation.walkthrough: Pater looks like father or a priest; it is Walter Pater, author of The Renaissance, whose first name loses its W.
explanation.definitionFit: To convert something is to change it, and alter is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Wild speed artist to perform. Bravo!

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters run riot into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
RA, Royal Academician, is an artist
to do is to perform

explanation.surface: Applause for a racing painter who performs at breakneck pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bravo!' reads as a cheer, but a bravo is a hired thug.
explanation.definitionFit: A bravo is a hired ruffian or bandit, and a desperado is a reckless outlaw.

clue.text: Insult a forward line in speech

indicators.note: in speech means the words are to be heard spoken, not read on the page

parts.note: a front is the forward line of an army

explanation.surface: Someone speaking rudely about a team's attacking line.
explanation.definitionFit: An affront is a deliberate slight or offence, a synonym for an insult.

clue.text: 3 3 on the watch

indicators.note: the first cross-reference stands for the clue word Convert, which tells us to change the letters around

parts.note: the second cross-reference stands for the answer to 3-down

explanation.surface: A bare pair of cross-references followed by a watchman's state.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 3 is read as 3-down's definition, Convert; the second as its answer, so ALTER is converted.
explanation.definitionFit: To be alert is to be watchful and ready, which is being on the watch.

clue.text: Like birds or oars skimming the water

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a rowing term for blades turned flat as they pass over the surface

explanation.walkthrough: In rowing, oars are turned horizontal between strokes so they skim the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds are plumed creatures, and rowers turn blades flat between strokes, so both are described by the same past participle.

clue.text: Otherwise the German Command

parts.note: or means otherwise, as in do it or else
der is German for the

explanation.surface: A warning about the German high command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Command' looks like the military noun for the German leadership; here it is an instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: An order is an instruction to be obeyed, the same as a command.

clue.text: They must accept blame for the treatment

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: taken as written
to take the rap is to accept blame

explanation.surface: Wrongdoers having to take responsibility for how someone was handled.
explanation.definitionFit: Therapy is medical or psychological treatment intended to heal.

clue.text: Form of rustic 14 holding a precious weight

indicators.note: holding means one piece clasps the other inside it

parts.note: 14 is transport, and a farm cart is a rustic form of it
taken as written

explanation.surface: A country vehicle laden with something valuable.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference sends you to 14-down, TRANSPORT; the rustic kind is a CART, which holds A.
explanation.definitionFit: A carat is the unit of mass used for weighing gems, so it is the weight of precious stones.

clue.text: Absquatulate — a slip of the tongue, bad

indicators.note: of the tongue says the word is as pronounced, here a careless spoken version

parts.note: a skid is a slip, spoken with a clipped vowel
an addle egg is a rotten, bad one

explanation.surface: A long, comic word followed by an apology for a bad verbal slip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A slip of the tongue' looks like a lapse in speech; it is a skid said aloud. Addle as an adjective means rotten, as in an addled egg.
explanation.definitionFit: Absquatulate is jocular American slang for running off or decamping, the same as skedaddle.

clue.text: Design confines me, after completion of murder, to hiding the body

indicators.note: confines means one word shuts the others up inside it

parts.note: a design is an intent or purpose

indicators.note: the completion of a word is its final letter, so only the end is kept

parts.note: the closing letter of murder
taken as written

explanation.surface: A killer's plan to conceal the corpse once the deed is done.
explanation.walkthrough: The order of the inserted letters follows the clue: me comes after the end of murder, and both go inside the design.
explanation.definitionFit: Interment is burial, putting a corpse in the ground, which hides the body.

clue.text: Jute sounds huskier

indicators.note: sounds says we want a word that is heard like the next one

parts.note: huskier means more hoarse, of a voice

explanation.surface: A sack of jute fibre making a rougher noise.
explanation.walkthrough: Jute looks like the fibre, but it is a member of the Germanic tribe; Horsa and Hengist were the Jutish leaders said to have landed in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: Horsa was a legendary chief of the Jutes who invaded Britain, so he is a Jute.

clue.text: under twenty-one

parts.note: surface reading: someone not yet of age, a minor in the old British sense when majority came at twenty-one
setter's reading: a whole number smaller than twenty-one, one of the five-letter ones

explanation.walkthrough: The page prints only these words, starting in lower case, so the clue's opening was probably lost in typesetting. As printed, the crossings fix a five-letter number below twenty-one; any wordplay in the missing words cannot be recovered.
explanation.definitionFit: Eight is a number less than twenty-one, the only five-letter number that fits the crossing letters E, G and T.

clue.text: Convey ecstasy

definitions.meaning: first meaning: carry from one place to another
second meaning: a state of rapture

explanation.walkthrough: The verb and the noun share a spelling; the noun is often plural, transports of joy.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means carry; as a noun it means an overwhelming emotion such as rapture.

clue.text: Hard luck — confound it — very sad

indicators.note: to confound is to throw into confusion, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone cursing their bad fortune and feeling miserable.
explanation.definitionFit: Adversity is misfortune or difficult circumstances, an equivalent of hard luck.

clue.text: Composer put on French grey green coat

parts.note: Giuseppe Verdi, the Italian opera composer
gris is French for grey

explanation.surface: A composer wearing a grey-green jacket in the French style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coat' looks like clothing; it is a coating on metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdigris is the green film that forms on copper and brass, a coating of green.

clue.text: Like the writings found in Cheddar

definitions.text: Like the writings found in Cheddar

parts.words: Like the writings found in Cheddar
parts.note: surface reading: some texts discovered in the Somerset town known for cheese
setter's reading: the Old Norse Edda sits inside the letters of Cheddar

explanation.walkthrough: Cheddar is a Somerset village famous for cheese, but here it is just a string of letters holding EDDA, the medieval collection of Norse poems.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eddas are medieval texts written down in Iceland, so being like them means being of that northern island.

clue.text: Display a stern hair-style

parts.note: pomp is grand display
taken as written
dour means stern and severe

explanation.surface: Showing off a severe haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: A pompadour is a hairstyle with the hair swept up high from the forehead, named after Madame de Pompadour.

clue.text: Bill and he follow Peter in the grand manner

indicators.note: follow says these pieces come after the other one, placing Peter's piece first

parts.note: Peter Pan, the boy who never grew up
AC, short for account, is a bill
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two people walking behind Peter with great style.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill looks like a man's name alongside Peter; it is an account, abbreviated in the usual way.
explanation.definitionFit: Panache is flamboyant style and confidence, a grand manner of doing things.

clue.text: "The glory and the —", Wordsworth missed

parts.note: surface reading: a quotation with its last word blanked out
setter's reading: the poet lamented losing this, so the missing word is the thing he missed

explanation.walkthrough: The quotation is from Wordsworth's Immortality Ode: 'Whither is fled the visionary gleam? Where is it now, the glory and the dream?' He mourns its loss, so it is what he missed.
explanation.definitionFit: The fill-in word completes the famous line, and the poem is about the vision of childhood the poet has lost.

clue.text: Eminent conductor is crazy — most are

indicators.note: crazy means mad and disordered, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wry remark that most great conductors are mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Maestro is the honorific for a distinguished conductor or musician.

clue.text: Steals jugs

definitions.meaning: first meaning: slang for pinches or takes
second meaning: slang for prisons, as jug is

explanation.walkthrough: Jugs looks like pitchers; it is the slang for jails.
explanation.definitionFit: Nick is British slang both for stealing and for a prison or police station, so the plural works for both.

clue.text: Rest wrong way round in hammock

indicators.note: the wrong way round means read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the following word

parts.note: letters from inside the word

explanation.surface: Lying in a hammock the wrong way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rest' looks like lying down; it is a pause in writing.
explanation.definitionFit: A comma marks a short pause in a sentence, a rest for the reader.

clue.text: Fix position of nothing, nothing, in French gallery

parts.note: O is zero, nothing
rien is French for nothing
the Tate is the London art gallery

explanation.surface: Trying to place something amid the emptiness of a French art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'in French' attaches to the second nothing only; the gallery is the Tate in London.
explanation.definitionFit: To orientate is to find or fix one's position relative to surroundings.

clue.text: Full of gin in the bar? What a nerve!

definitions.text: Full of gin in the bar?
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the measuring device fixed to an upturned spirit bottle in a pub
second meaning: the nerve carrying signals from the eye

explanation.walkthrough: In British pubs spirits are poured through an optic, a dispenser that gives an exact measure. 'What a nerve!' reads as outrage.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a bar's spirit-measuring device and the nerve of sight.

clue.text: More precise definition — I certainly provide it

indicators.note: the words provide it means they supply the letters themselves, within them

parts.note: letters running across the end of one word, a lone letter and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A pedant promising to give a tighter definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Nice in its older sense means fine or precise, as in a nice distinction.

clue.text: Job having one — against ill winds ?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Bible's Job had friends whose consolation only made him feel worse
second meaning: a long woollen scarf worn to keep out cold, harmful winds

explanation.walkthrough: A Job's comforter is someone who makes things worse while trying to console; a comforter is also an old word for a long woollen scarf.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a consoler, as with Job's false friends, and a warm scarf that protects against bitter weather.

clue.text: Younger son's a bounder — and in France, too !

parts.note: a cad or bounder is an ill-mannered man
et is French for and

explanation.surface: A disreputable younger son, one who behaves badly in France too.
explanation.walkthrough: A bounder is an old British word for a cad, a man of bad behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Cadet originally means a younger son of a family, as against the eldest, the heir.

clue.text: With spring, last ice melts

indicators.note: melting things lose their shape, so these letters reform in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: As the season turns, the last of the winter ice thaws.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With spring' reads as a time of year; it means having springiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Something elastic is springy, returning to shape after stretching, so it has spring.

clue.text: Wind interior of microcosm into knots

indicators.note: tied into knots means twisted and tangled, so the letters are muddled
the interior of a word is everything but its outside letters

parts.note: the word without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A small world twisted up by a gale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' could be the verb to twist; it is the noun, a named wind.
explanation.definitionFit: The sirocco is a hot wind blowing from North Africa across the Mediterranean.
